chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Ismail ibn Mihran

key_terms.إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ مِهْرَانَ: Ismail ibn Mihran — a well-known narrator who transmitted from Imam al-Ridha (AS) and appears in multiple chains in al-Kafi
key_terms.مِثْلَهُ: similar to it — a technical hadith term indicating this isnad transmits the same matn as the preceding hadith

ai.seo_question: What does 'mithluhu' (similar to it) mean in hadith literature?
ai.summary: This hadith is a parallel transmission (مِثْلَهُ — 'similar to it') referring back to the preceding hadith (no. 3) in the chapter on concealing testimony. It provides an alternative chain of narrators — Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, and Ismail ibn Mihran — for the same teaching reported from Imam al-Hassan al-'Askari (AS) about establishing testimony for God's sake. In classical hadith methodology, such parallel transmission strengthens the authenticity of the original report by showing it was preserved through multiple independent chains.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al Nahdy, from Ismail Bin Mihran
